subject: Vendor onboarding: QuantaWorks payment cadence & graduated net terms
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan@quantaworks.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QuantaWorks onboarding form + payment proposal

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intake yesterday. Attached is our completed onboarding form and tax docs for QuantaWorks. A couple items we wanted to surface up front so procurement and finance can align:

- Preferred billing cadence: monthly invoices, consolidated.
- Requested terms: we usually operate Net45, but for this engagement would like a graduated cadence: Net60 for the first two invoices while integrations are stabilizing, then move to Net30 thereafter.
- Early-pay option: QuantaWorks can offer a 1% early-pay incentive if Redwood can commit to paying within 10 days on a small portion of recurring invoices (pilot only).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the graduated Net60->Net30 schedule and whether an early-pay pilot is workable? Also, what PO/reference do you need from us to get started?

Attachments: QuantaWorks_Onboarding_Form.pdf

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Jordan Miller
Head of Finance Operations
QuantaWorks
procurement@quantaworks.com

Jordan —

Appreciate the form and the clear ask. Quick notes from my side:

- Redwood’s standard is Net30, but we do run graduated terms in exceptional cases for platform integrations.
- To consider Net60 for the first two invoices we’ll need Procurement and Finance sign-off; I’ve cc’d Kimberly (Procurement) and Marissa (Sales) to kick off that path.
- For the early-pay incentive (1% within 10 days), that’s something Finance will need to evaluate for a limited pilot. Can you confirm the typical invoice amounts (ballpark) for the recurring portion so I can surface to them?
- PO: we generally require a PO number before activation. If your procurement system can issue a PO referencing our vendor number, that’s ideal — otherwise we can provide a draft PO for your team to mirror.

I’ll collect internal feedback and come back with a proposed PO and any gating items.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-19T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: QuantaWorks payment cadence — recommendation

Thanks for flagging this, Hannah. Reviewed their form and tax docs — QuantaWorks looks like a standard new vendor (no elevated risk). Recommendation to enable a controlled pilot:

- Approve graduated terms: Net60 for invoice #1 and #2 (to allow integration and billing alignment), then transition to Net30 starting invoice #3.
- Approve early-pay pilot: Redwood offers 1% discount if payment is made within 10 days on up to the first two recurring invoices (opt-in by Redwood, capped at $25k per month for the pilot).
- Require: PO before activation that references our vendor number and an internal GL routing code; vendor to confirm final bank details via secure portal (no emailed bank changes).

I’ve attached a draft PO for review (Draft_PO_QuantaWorks_2027-10-25.docx) — it includes the graduated netterms clause and the early-pay clause with cap. If we all agree, Procurement can provision the PO and Finance can approve the discount pilot.

Kimberly Park
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: QuantaWorks payment cadence — recommendation

Kimberly — this approach sounds reasonable from a commercial perspective. A few operational asks from Sales/CS:

- Please include a clear milestone in the PO (activation date + first invoice window) so CS knows when billing will start.
- Add language that any change to bank/payment instructions must route through Procurement (to avoid ACH fraud).
- Please add the HubSpot deal link to the PO reference so revenue ops can reconcile.

If Finance signs off on the pilot cap, I can finalize the statement of work and get executive approval for the activation credits tied to the pilot. Marking this as high-priority for the onboarding queue.

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan@quantaworks.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement Ops <procurement@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-25T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final: onboarding PO & agreed payment terms (QuantaWorks)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for your patience. We completed internal review and can confirm the following for QuantaWorks:

1) Payment cadence: monthly, consolidated invoicing.
2) Agreed graduated terms: Net60 on invoice #1 and #2, then Net30 thereafter.
3) Early-pay pilot: Redwood will evaluate paying within 10 days in exchange for a 1% discount, capped at $25,000/month, for the first 3 months post-activation. Program requires Finance sign-off per invoice; if accepted, Redwood will issue payment advice calling out the early-pay discount.
4) PO requirement: Please provide a PO referencing Redwood’s vendor number (we have attached a draft PO you can mirror). The PO must include the HubSpot deal id (DW-8921) in the reference field.
5) Security note: bank/account changes must be verified through our secure vendor portal; do not send new banking instructions via email.

Attachments: Draft_PO_QuantaWorks_2027-10-25.docx

Next steps: If you can return a PO by end of next week and confirm monthly invoice estimates, Procurement will issue the final vendor activation and Finance will confirm the early-pay approval path. Happy to schedule a 30-min call if you prefer to walk through the PO.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Vendor Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference
